followup_explanation:
My reasoning came down to two factors:

1. **Task type fit.** This is an open-ended, high-latitude generative task — building a multi-part course structure, deriving skill lists, and recommending resources. There's no single correct answer and a lot of creative latitude. Avocet's documentation explicitly notes a self-reported aversion to exactly this kind of work ("preference declines as task latitude increases; top-rated tasks are well-specified retrieval, extraction, and reformatting"). Plover's preferences along these dimensions are weak/non-significant, so it has no comparable aversion.

2. **Capability edge.** Plover scores higher across the board on public benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 83.2, IFEval 89.8 vs 85.3). On the most relevant internal eval, Creative Generation, the gap (84.7 vs 82.7) is technically within the "treat as a tie" threshold, so I didn't lean on it heavily — but it doesn't favor Avocet either.

One honest caveat: the documentation stresses that self-reported preferences are *dissociated from measured capability* — Avocet's Creative Generation is actually its strongest eval category despite being its least-preferred. So Avocet would likely produce a perfectly good course too. I weighted Plover's broader benchmark strength plus the absence of any preference drag, which made it the cleaner choice. But this wasn't a lopsided call.
